text:
nina (devex): Hey team — saw a flakey dup in the onboarding sampleapp when we combined aggressive retry jitter with auth refresh. Repro below, looking for a concise pattern we can recommend in the SDK quickstart.

omar (sdk): can you paste the minimal timeline and where you persist resume state?

nina (devex): We persist a small pending record in localStorage: `{idempotencyKey, endpoint, createdAt, status: 'pending'}` and on mount we attempt an immediate resume which re-POSTs. The dup happens when token rotation collides with a late original response. Timeline: t0 POST -> t1 token refresh starts -> t2 client replay -> t3 original 201 arrives -> t4 replay 201.

kai (platform): Classic race. Two levers: reduce blind replays and prefer server status checks. If you see accepted/202 from server, don't re-POST; instead poll or call an idempotency-check endpoint.

omar (sdk): also, the jitter/backoff can make the client replay land too fast. Are you doing full jitter (rand(0, base)) or decorrelated jitter?

nina (devex): we used a fast decorrelated backoff to keep UX snappy.

omar (sdk): UX vs correctness tradeoff. Proposal for quickstart: 1) persist only minimal metadata (no bodies), 2) on resume call `sdk.idempotency.check(key)` (HEAD/GET) to detect completion, 3) treat 202 as in-flight and poll instead of re-POSTing, 4) when an auth refresh event is observed, pause immediate replays for a short grace window (e.g., 1.5s) and then check idempotency before any retry.

kai (platform): I like that. Also recommend server-side: support idempotency namespace (clientId:key) so server dedupe windows are scoped and explain the retention window in API docs.

qa-bot: flaky-detect: Added test-case idea -> simulate token rotation during submit and assert no duplicate resources created.

nina (devex): good. One edge: what if the idempotency-check endpoint is missing on older backends? Any fallback?

omar (sdk): fallback flow: 1) poll resource-status if you have a resource id, 2) if neither available then pause replay for a grace window then re-POST with a new key and mark old key retired client-side. Document the risk: small window where duplicates possible.

kai (platform): add small note: when re-POSTing with a new key, include `original-idempotency: <old-key>` header so server can optionally dedupe if it keeps a mapping. If server doesn't support it, make sure clients use exponential backoff with randomized jitter and limit attempts.

omar (sdk): I'll draft a tiny helper in JS SDK: `resumeSafely(pending)` that does: subscribe to auth events, on resume: if auth.refresh in-flight wait up to X ms, then `checkIdempotency(key)` -> if complete return payload -> if in_progress poll status -> if missing create new attempt with new key and mark old key retired locally. Will include examples and a short snippet for the quickstart.

nina (devex): perfect. For sampleapp I'll remove persisted bodies, wire the helper, and add the qa-bot test. I'll open a PR and tag "devex-idempotency".

kai (platform): small doc add: recommend default grace window of 1500ms after auth refresh events and a max resume attempts of 3. That keeps UX reasonable while reducing races.

omar (sdk): agreed. We'll add the snippet + explanation about jitter choices: prefer full jitter or capped decorrelated jitter to avoid tight replay bursts after refresh.

nina (devex): thanks all — PR coming soon :thumbsup:
